comparison: Both evaluate claims C26-31 about experimental evolution producing clumpy phenotypes. OpenEval finds the data strongly supportive, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to missing prospective control (parallel evolution in non-sucrose environment). Reviewers acknowledge 'excellent dataset' but consider lack of control a significant limitation despite post hoc analyses.

Both evaluate claims C11, C17-18, C21-25 about engineered strategies enabling growth in low sucrose. Complete agreement - both find the experimental data (Figures 1-2, Table 1) supportive. Peer reviewers do not raise concerns about these engineered strain experiments.

Both evaluate claims C81-85, C118-119 about differential selection in sucrose vs. monosaccharide media. Complete agreement - both find evidence supportive. Peer reviewers explicitly call these post hoc analyses 'the most compelling' evidence for sucrose-specific fitness increase, though they wished for prospective controls.

Both evaluate claims C71-80 about recreation/reversion experiments validating causal mutations. OpenEval finds validation rigorous and supportive, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN because recreated strains are less fit than evolved clones, suggesting 'something is being missed' (possibly copy number variation).

Both evaluate claims C12-16, C36-37 about invertase expression and dependence on secreted invertase. OpenEval finds RNA-seq and competition data supportive. Peer reviewers also accept these findings as part of 'excellent dataset' without specific concerns. Peer result also includes C34-35 (clump formation mechanism).

Both address genomic analysis claims. OpenEval R5 covers C38-39, C106-108 (whole genome sequencing methodology). Peer R3 covers broader set including mutations in multiple pathways (C38-39, C42-44, C47-48, C54-55, C61, C64-65, C68-69, C106, C108). OpenEval supportive; peer reviewers UNCERTAIN, wanting tetrad dissection for more definitive statements and concerned about possible copy number variation.

Both evaluate claims C87-89 about antagonistic pleiotropy and fitness trade-offs. Complete agreement - both find evidence supportive. Peer reviewers do not challenge these trade-off findings, consistent with evolutionary theory.

Both evaluate claims C90-92 about genotype-phenotype relationships from allelic combination analysis. OpenEval finds RT-qPCR and microscopy data supportive. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, suggesting 'simple tetrad dissection would enable more definitive statements' about causal relationships.

Both evaluate claims C109-111 about RNA-seq showing downregulation of cell separation genes in clumpy clones. Complete agreement - both find evidence supportive. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings.

Both evaluate claims C112-113 about dependence on secreted invertase ruling out sucrose import. Complete agreement - both find competition data and RT-qPCR supportive. Peer reviewers treat this as straightforward validation of public goods mechanism.

Both evaluate claims about synergistic effects of multiple strategies (C120-126 overlap). OpenEval finds reasoning logical and well-supported (though notes C129 speculation not directly tested). Peer reviewers accept the synergistic interpretation without challenge.

Partial overlap on claims about monosaccharide controls. OpenEval R14 covers C86, C114-117 (lack of fitness advantage in monosaccharide, multicellularity necessary but not sufficient). Peer R5 covers broader differential selection claims C81-85, C114-119. Both supportive, though addressing somewhat different aspects.

Both address broader implications for multicellularity evolution. OpenEval R20 covers C93, C96-98 (public goods hypothesis support) rated SUPPORTED with note that C96 is somewhat speculative. Peer R12 covers C93, C96-105 rated UNCERTAIN, wanting more discussion of general implications and whether system oversimplifies multicellularity evolution.

Both address evolutionary implications and mechanisms. OpenEval R21 covers C99-103 (target size, recurrent selection speculation) rated SUPPORTED though noting some speculation. Peer R12 covers C93, C96-105 rated UNCERTAIN, asking for clearer discussion of whether findings have direct implications for multicellularity evolution and noting clumpiness likely evolved multiple times in yeast.

Partial overlap on speculative evolutionary claims. OpenEval R22 covers C94-95, C104-105 rated UNCERTAIN as speculative extrapolations lacking direct experimental support. Peer R12 covers broader implications C93, C96-105 also rated UNCERTAIN, wanting more nuanced discussion of evolutionary interpretation.

Minor overlap on clump formation mechanism. OpenEval R3 covers C32-35 (two-color fluorescence showing incomplete separation) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes C34-35 among broader characterization claims, also rated SUPPORTED without specific concerns.

Minor overlap on loss-of-function mutations. OpenEval R6 covers C40-45 (nonsense mutations, cell separation gene expression) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C42-44 among broader genomic analysis rated UNCERTAIN, wanting additional validation beyond bulk segregant analysis.

Minor overlap on N-end rule pathway. OpenEval R7 covers C46-50 (mutations in ACE2, AXL1, UBR1, RAD6) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C47-48 among broader genomic claims rated UNCERTAIN, wanting tetrad dissection for more definitive statements.

Minor overlap on glucose sensing pathway. OpenEval R8 covers C51-58 (MTH1, RGT1, SNF3 mutations) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C54-55 among broader genomic analysis rated UNCERTAIN, suggesting tetrad dissection would strengthen conclusions.

Minor overlap on cAMP pathway. OpenEval R9 covers C59-63 (IRA1, IRA2 mutations) rated SUPPORTED though noting direct cAMP measurement would strengthen conclusions. Peer R3 includes C61 among broader genomic claims rated UNCERTAIN.

Minor overlap on SIN4/mediator complex. OpenEval R10 covers C64-68 (SIN4 mutations, HXT3 upregulation) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C64-65, C68 among broader genomic analysis rated UNCERTAIN, wanting additional validation.

Minor overlap on gene amplification. OpenEval R11 covers C69-70 (HXT6/7 amplification) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C69 among broader genomic claims rated UNCERTAIN, with concern about possible copy number variation being missed.

OpenEval R23 evaluates background claims C1-4 (prior literature on multicellularity evolution, public goods) rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are contextual claims not specifically addressed by reviewers.

OpenEval R24 evaluates background claims C5-10 (invertase function, diffusion physics, mechanistic rationale) rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these establish theoretical foundation not specifically questioned by reviewers.

OpenEval R25 evaluates background claims C19-20 (MAL genes in S288c strain) rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - this is technical background information not addressed by reviewers.
